  3. Link RCS-26978 as "relates to" for history — this is a pattern with this user.

  4. Izenda category visibility on PC vs. mobile is typically a role/permission rendering difference in how Izenda loads the category tree, or a browser caching issue. Since it resolved itself last time without any admin changes, a cache/browser refresh is the first path before any backend investigation.

Updated Analysis

This is not a browser cache issue and not a transient problem. The screenshot tells a very specific story.

What's actually missing on PC: The categories that are absent are exactly the ones that contain incident report categories — "3-Incident Report- External Theft", "4-Internal Theft", "Burglary", "0- Sales Audit", "Z-Archive", "zOther Canned." These are incident-type report categories. The categories that do show are primarily audit-related.

The pattern: Phone shows the full list including incident report folders. PC shows a truncated list missing the incident/theft categories. This is consistent with what Yannick clarified in RCS-26978: "I see the audits, not the incident reports."

Most likely cause: Izenda role/category permissions are rendering differently between the desktop browser and mobile browser. This is a known Izenda behavior — if a user's role has access to multiple category types, the desktop Izenda UI can sometimes fail to render all top-level categories if there's a rendering width/scroll issue, OR if the user's role assignment changed between sessions. The fact that the phone shows more categories than the PC (not fewer) points away from a permissions gap and toward a UI rendering/scroll truncation issue on the desktop Izenda left panel.

Key observation: The PC left panel has a scrollbar — it's possible the missing categories exist but the panel is truncating the list and the user isn't scrolling far enough down, OR the category tree isn't fully loading. On mobile, the full list is visible in a dropdown/modal that shows all at once.

Revised Next Steps

  1. Ask Yannick to scroll down in the left Categories panel on PC — the panel has a scrollbar visible in the screenshot. Categories like "0-Sales Audit", "3-Incident Report-External Theft", "4-Internal Theft", "Burglary", "Z-Archive", "zOther Canned" may simply be above the visible area (the list appears to start at "0-Operation Audit" — "0-Sales Audit" alphabetically comes before it, which would mean it's scrolled off the top).

  2. Actually — looking more carefully: "0-Sales Audit" should appear above "0-Operation Audit" alphabetically. The PC list starts at "0-Operation Audit" and has a scrollbar at the top of the list — Yannick may be scrolled down and not see the categories above the fold. Have him scroll to the very top of the Categories panel.

  3. If scrolling doesn't explain it (some categories like "3-Incident Report-External Theft" should appear between "2-" and "4-" and are definitely missing mid-list), then check Yannick's role/category access in Izenda Admin on pd-lpms-iis-015 — the role may have a category filter applied that behaves differently between browser contexts.

  4. Do not escalate to engineering yet — this is a frontend/config investigation first.

Good. Here's the full picture with skills applied:

Yes — This Could Absolutely Be Permissions. Here's the Diagnostic Breakdown.

The Izenda forensic skill classifies this as Category 4 — "Different Results, Same Query" — the most telling pattern being: same user, different device, different category list. That maps directly to one of two causes: user-level permission filtering, or a browser rendering issue. The screenshot now lets us get specific.

What the Screenshot Actually Shows

PC is missing mid-list categories — specifically between "2-" and "5 Internal Audit":

  • 0-Sales Audit (missing — would be above "0-Operation Audit")

  • 3-Incident Report- External Theft

  • 4-Internal Theft

  • Burglary

  • Z-Archive

  • zOther Canned (+ subcategories)

These are incident report categories. The ones that show on PC are primarily audit categories. This is not random truncation — there's a clear pattern. Incident = missing. Audit = visible.

Could This Be Permissions Set Up This Way Intentionally?

Yes, absolutely. Izenda category visibility is controlled by the user's Role in Izenda Admin. If Yannick has two different accounts — one on PC, one on mobile — and they're assigned different Izenda roles, this exact result is possible and expected. One role has access to both audit and incident report categories; the other only has audit categories.

The Username Question — This Is the Key Ask

We don't know yet whether he's using the same login on both devices. This is the first thing to nail down. From the screenshot:

  • The PC shows a category called "Yannick Labelle- Report" — this is a personal folder, meaning Izenda knows who he is on PC

  • The phone also shows "Yannick Labelle- Report" — same personal folder visible on phone

That's a strong signal it is the same user account on both. But we still need to confirm — Yannick may have two separate netTrack logins (e.g. ylabelle on PC and yannick.labelle on mobile), or he may be using SSO on one and a direct login on the other.

What to Do — In Order

  1. Ask Yannick directly (draft below):

What is the username you use to log in on your PC laptop? And what username are you using on your phone? (They may be the same — just confirming.)

  1. If same username — look at Izenda Role assignment in the Izenda Admin panel on pd-lpms-iis-015:

  • Navigate to [pvh prod URL]/izenda/

  • Go to Settings → Security → Roles

  • Find Yannick's assigned role

  • Check what Categories are exposed to that role

  • If categories like "3-Incident Report" are not checked for his role, that's the answer — it's a permission configuration, not a bug

  1. If different usernames — look up both in dbo.LPUser on pd-lpms-iis-015:

sql

SELECT UserID, LoginID, FirstName, LastName, Inactive, SecurityID, StoreIdent\nFROM dbo.LPUser\nWHERE LoginID LIKE '%yannick%'\n   OR LoginID LIKE '%labelle%'\n   OR EmailAddr LIKE '%yannicklabelle%'

Then compare the SecurityID on both records — if they point to different security roles, the Izenda category visibility would differ between them.

  1. Check if this is intentional config vs. a misconfiguration — it's possible a previous support engineer or admin intentionally restricted his PC-browser role to audit categories only, and the phone is accessing a different auth path that gives him broader access.

Draft Client Reply

Hi Yannick,

Thank you for the screenshot — that's very helpful. Looking at the comparison, I can see specific categories are missing on your PC that are visible on your phone, particularly the incident report categories.

Before I investigate further, could you confirm: what is the username you use to log in on your PC laptop? And is it the same username you use on your phone, or a different one? This will help me determine whether the difference is related to your account permissions.

Thank you, Tyrone

Bottom line: This smells like either a role-permission difference between two logins, or a single login whose Izenda role was configured with audit categories only. The "Yannick Labelle- Report" personal folder appearing on both devices leans toward same user — but the missing incident categories are too clean and too specific to be a browser issue. Get the username confirmation first, then go to Izenda Admin.

Engineering Escalation — Intermittent Errors Post-Migration (Azure Host)

Following today's testing in the test environment, reports and filters are functioning when accessed through the proper platform entry point. However, intermittent 500 errors are still occurring and will continue to affect Yannick in production until the following are addressed.

Root Cause: CustomAdHocConfig.InitializeReporting() at CustomAdHoc.vb line 673 is throwing a null reference when the Izenda report list page is accessed directly or without a warm platform session. This is a cold start / session context problem introduced by the Azure migration — the legacy IIS environment held session state persistently at the server level, masking this issue. Azure App Services recycles app pools and spins up new instances, dropping session context and exposing the unguarded null reference.

What Yannick Will Experience Until Fixed: Intermittent 500 errors on report access — unpredictable from his perspective, most likely on first access of the day or after periods of inactivity. This will generate repeat tickets.

Recommended Engineering Actions Before Production Push:

  1. Null guard at CustomAdHoc.vb line 673 — InitializeReporting() should check for null before proceeding and redirect cleanly to /pvh/platform instead of throwing a 500

  2. Session state persistence — Configure sticky sessions or distributed session state (Redis or Azure SQL) on the Azure App Service so session context survives app pool recycles

  3. Always On — Verify the Always On setting is enabled on the PVH Azure App Service to prevent cold starts

  4. Entry point enforcement — Direct URL hits to Izenda should validate that platform initialization has occurred and redirect gracefully if not, rather than assuming session context is present

Current Workaround: Navigating back to the platform home (https://apps.apprissretail.com/pvh/platform) and re-entering warms the session and resolves the error for that session. Back button also works if the error is hit mid-session.

Recommendation: These items should be resolved before today's production push. In current state, Yannick will hit the cold start error on first access tomorrow morning and this ticket will reopen.

— Tyrone Whitney

Problem 2 — SQL syntax error on "Internal Theft by position"

This is a hard database error, not a data gap. The error text you pasted is explicit:

Incorrect syntax near the keyword 'AS'. Incorrect syntax near the keyword 'with'. If this statement is a common table expression... the previous statement must be terminated with a semicolon.

That's repeated five times — five separate CTEs (Common Table Expressions) in the same query are all failing. What this means: the Internal Theft by position report part uses CTEs — SQL blocks that look like WITH cte_name AS (SELECT...). On the old platform this worked. On the new platform, Izenda is generating SQL where the statement preceding each CTE isn't being terminated with a semicolon, which is required in SQL Server for CTEs. This is either a SQL Server version difference between old and new platform, or Izenda's query generator is producing subtly different SQL under Platform Cohesion that violates the new server's stricter parsing.

Problem 3 — rs.aspx?previewResults=-1

Look at the F12 capture — rs.aspx?previewResults=-1 returned 6.0 kB in 815ms. Negative one preview results is Izenda's way of saying "render all rows, no limit." That fired and returned data — 6 kB — which means the server responded. But the charts still show zero. That disconnect between data being returned by the server and zero chart results on screen points to a rendering/mapping issue — the data is coming back but Izenda can't plot it, likely because the field names or data types changed in the new schema.

96 requests, 21.9 kB transferred, 1.8 MB resources, finished in 7.36 seconds. Page loads fine. No 302s, no routing issues. This is not a Yarp problem at all — PVH's issues are purely database and SQL generation layer. Completely different root cause from Tailored Brands.

What the Izenda/report-side person CAN fix

If you have someone with deep Izenda report designer access — what you're calling the Izenda expert — they can potentially fix the Internal Theft by position section at the report level without touching the server. Here's how:

The CTE error is happening because the SQL Izenda generates for that report part starts a WITH block without a semicolon terminating the previous statement. An Izenda-savvy person could go into the Data Sources tab of that report, look at how the position pivot is constructed, and either rewrite the expression to avoid CTEs entirely — using subqueries or derived tables instead — or add the missing semicolon termination in a custom SQL override if Izenda exposes that option for that report type.

They could also potentially rebuild the Internal Theft by position chart using a different aggregation approach that doesn't require CTEs at all — GROUP BY with a positional field instead of a ranked CTE. Same output, different SQL path, no compatibility issue.

That's a legitimate fix path and it doesn't require Engineering or a server config change.

What ONLY a backend fix can solve

The SQL Server compatibility level issue is broader than just this one report. Every report PVH has that uses CTEs — and there may be others beyond this one — will hit the same wall. Fixing it report by report is whack-a-mole. The server-side fix sets the compatibility level once and resolves the entire class of problem permanently for PVH and every other PC-mode client on that same SQL Server instance.

The other things that can't be fixed at the report level:

The Quirks Mode rendering and the deprecated CSS — those are baked into Izenda's application code. No report configuration touches that. That's a codebase issue.

The language preference not persisting between deploys — that's a session/profile storage issue at the platform layer. No report config fixes that.

The export delivery issues from Tailored Brands — the 302 Yarp routing gap — zero report configuration can address that. That lives entirely in the proxy config.

The practical recommendation

Send the Internal Theft by position problem to the Izenda expert first. Give them the exact error, the report name, the section name, and the explanation that the fix is either rewriting the position pivot to avoid CTEs or adding a semicolon termination before the WITH clause in the custom SQL. If they can fix it at the report level in a day, that's faster than waiting for Engineering to schedule a SQL Server compatibility level change.

But flag to Engineering in parallel that the compatibility level needs to be addressed anyway — because the next migrated client who has a CTE-based report will hit the same error and there won't always be an Izenda expert available to rewrite it report by report.

Two-track approach: Izenda expert fixes the immediate PVH symptom, Engineering fixes the underlying platform condition. Both are valid, neither is a substitute for the other.

INTERNAL NOTE

Finding: CTE Syntax Error on PVH Izenda Incident Reports — Resolved via Save As

Summary: Post-Platform Cohesion migration, PVH Izenda reports sourced from incident data throw repeated CTE syntax errors on both render and export. Audit-based reports are unaffected. The root cause is stale compiled SQL in the original report definitions from pre-migration — not missing views or schema objects.

Replication Steps to Fix:

  1. Open the broken report in Izenda (e.g., 0- Internal Theft Report-2025- Employee Information)

  2. Click Save As — give it a new name (no field or filter changes needed)

  3. Run the saved copy — incident data, employee fields, and amounts all populate correctly

  4. Confirm export also works on the new copy

Why This Works: Save As forces Izenda to regenerate the report's SQL from the current field definitions against the active incident schema. The original reports carry cached/compiled SQL from the pre-migration dbo schema, which no longer resolves — causing the CTE WITH clause failures. The new copy builds clean SQL and the error is eliminated.

Screenshot: TTW TEST copy of Employee Information report — all incident fields populating with live data after Save As, no code changes.

Scope: Any PVH report that was built pre-migration and sources incident data may need this treatment. Audit-based reports are not affected.
